newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-SMITH AWAITS HIS FATE IN 1,500 METRES FREESTYLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-SMITH AWAITS HIS FATE IN 1,500 METRES FREESTYLE.

text.p: Olympic bronze medallist Graeme Smith of Britain faced an unwanted wait on Sunday to learn his fate in the 1,500 metres freestyle on the last day of the world short-course swimming championships.

The programme's longest event is contested on the strength of heat times, with no final, and Smith had to swim in the morning session because of a slow submitted time, with his main rivals not entering the action until the evening session.
Smith won his heat on Sunday in 14 minutes 46.85 seconds, a time which would have given him the gold at the last world short-course championships in Rio de Janeiro in 1995.
He was not allowed to swim in the fastest seeded heat because his one race of the past year in a 25-metre pool was a relatively slow 15:27.47 at the British short-course championships last December.

Smith was not permitted to submit the 15:02.48 with which he took the Olympic bronze in Atlanta last July because that was achieved in a 50-metre long-course pool and he had a short-course time on record.
"I was really disappointed that nobody in the (British) association said I needed to do a short-course time," said Smith, who had imagined his Olympic time would count.
"If someone beats me by a few tenths (of a second) tonight I'll be very disappointed."
